note: Written in the everyday spoken Ma'di of Adjumani and Moyo, addressed to one person (mi), with the negative ku, the perfective 'bo and the implosive apostrophes of the standard orthography ('ba, 'di, e'yo). Ma'di and Lugbara share most of their Central Sudanic core (mu, emu, fe, le, ni, ti, jo, yi), so where a Ma'di-specific form was not certain the shared form was kept and the Ma'di variants that are certain were used instead (ndre for see, matuka for car, kiti for seat, kuru for now). Buttons are bare verbs: Tu (board), Awa (share), Kodi (rent), Pe (send). No native reviewer has read this: a Ma'di speaker should expect to replace a good share of the vocabulary that reads as Lugbara, and every paragraph is a close paraphrase rather than a sentence-by-sentence rendering.
